rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read الريح singular here; the other readers use the plural, with detailed distributions varying across the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي الريح على التوحيد والباقون على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far reads الرياح plural throughout except in al-Dhariyat; Abu Amr, Ya'qub, Ibn Amir, and Asim have it plural in ten specified locations.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر الرياح على الجمع كل القرآن إلا في الذاريات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi has twelve plural readings, Ibn Kathir five, and al-Kisa'i three; Hamza agrees with al-Kisa'i except in al-Hijr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع في اثني عشر موضعا هذه العشرة وفي إبراهيم وعسق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas associates plural winds with mercy and singular wind with punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس الرياح للرحمة والريح للعذاب

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed that a blowing wind be made merciful winds rather than a destructive wind.
rows.anchor: اللهم إجعلها رياحا ولا تجعلها ريحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophetic prayer likely alludes to winds sent as good news and to the barren wind sent against Aad; Qur'anic wording can mark a particular sense.
rows.anchor: ومن آياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali prefers plural الرياح because each wind is like the others as evidence of divine unity; singular can express a generic class, as in common sayings.
rows.anchor: وتصريف الرياح على الجمع أولى لأن كل واحدة من الرياح مثل الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular wind against Aad is one particular wind, supported by the parallel description as a violent, cold wind and by the report about the west wind.
rows.anchor: وفي عاد إذ أرسلنا عليهم الريح العقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic formula ما يدريك is generally left unexplained, unlike ما أدراك followed by an explanation; wording can signal whether the matter is disclosed.
rows.anchor: ما يدريك مبهم غير مبين وما كان من لفظ ما أدريك

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: A prophetic report says the east wind brought victory, while the west wind destroyed Aad, supporting a particular singular wind.
rows.anchor: نصرت بالصبا وأهلكت عاد بالدبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creation means bringing something into existence according to a measure without copying a model; only God can properly be called creator.
rows.anchor: الخلق هو الإحداث للشيء على تقدير من غير احتذاء على مثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars differ over خلق as a verbal noun: some take it as willing the thing; others as a name for an abstract, determined state such as existence or origination.
rows.anchor: واختلف أهل العلم فيه إذا كان بمعنى المصدر فقال قوم هو الإرادة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term creation can also denote the created object, just as رضا can denote what is approved, though source and created thing are not identical meanings.
rows.anchor: وقد استعمل الخلق بمعنى المخلوق كما استعمل الرضا بمعنى المرضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are plural because revelation identifies them as seven; saying earth in the singular avoids suggesting that one heaven alone is meant.
rows.anchor: وإنما السماوات ووحدت الأرض لأنه لما ذكر السماء بأنها سبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are not one uniform class: each has its own appropriate governance, whereas earth resembles one kind whose plural would imply differing kinds.
rows.anchor: وليس تجري السماوات مجرى الجنس المتفق لأنه دبر في كل سماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اختلاف means either the alternation of night and day, each following the other, or differences of kind such as black versus white.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو من اختلاف الجنس كاختلاف السواد والبياض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is darkness following day; day is expansive brightness. Night has a count noun, while day generally functions like a mass noun, though a rare plural occurs.
rows.anchor: والليل هو الظلام المعاقب للنهار واحدته ليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet's verb أنهرت witnesses the sense of making wide or opening broadly, applied to the widening of a tear in cloth.
rows.anchor: ملكت بها كفي فأنهرت فتقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الفلك names ships in either singular or plural; it also means the celestial orbit or any circular thing. The lexicographers differ whether it names rotation or the seven celestial layers.
rows.anchor: والفلك السفن تقع على الواحد والجمع والفلك فلك السماء

rows.speaker: صاحب العين
rows.claim: One lexical view takes الفلك to be the rotation itself; another takes it as the seven layers containing the stars.
rows.anchor: قيل هو اسم للدوران خاصة وقيل بل اسم الأطباق سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say السماء can mean clouds because anything above another is its sky; Ali ibn Isa says clouds may be vapors rising from earth, a possibility neither reason nor revelation rules out.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى: قيل إن السحاب بخارات تصعد من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The known heaven is the roof above earth, and the root of سماء conveys height; layers can be sky relative to what lies below and earth relative to what is above.
rows.anchor: فالسماء المعروفة سقف الأرض وأصله من السمو وهو العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sea is a broad expanse of water wider than a river; benefit is pleasure, joy, or what leads to either, and painful means can benefit when they yield pleasure.
rows.anchor: والبحر هو الخرق الواسع للماء الذي يزيد على سعة النهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Land lives through plant growth and dies through dryness; broadcasting means dispersing, and dabbah covers every created creeping thing though common usage means riding animals.
rows.anchor: وحياة الأرض عمارتها بالنبات وموتها خرابها بالجفاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تصريف is turning and varying; cloud is named for its dragging motion, while subjugation, taming, and making easy are near synonyms.
rows.anchor: والتصريف التقليب وصرف الدهر تقلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four winds are north, south, east, and west; their names and directions are defined in relation to the qibla, with intermediate winds between them.
rows.anchor: والرياح أربع الشمال والجنوب والصبا والدبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Broadcasting means dispersing, and grief is called بث because it divides and burdens the heart.
rows.anchor: والبث التفريق وكل شيء بثثته فقد فرقته

rows.speaker: أبو داود
rows.claim: Abu Dawud's verse describes clouds as impregnated and brought to rain by the south wind; للقح الجنوب means that the south wind impregnates them.
rows.anchor: لقحن ضحيا للقح الجنوب

rows.speaker: زهير
rows.claim: Zuhayr's verse calls the cold north wind مشمولة, reflecting that people dislike its cold and its dispersal of clouds; the term extends to anything disliked.
rows.anchor: نوى مشمولة فمتى اللقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage answers disbelievers asking what proves that their deity is one: the listed created phenomena are signs of one creator.
rows.anchor: لما أخبر الله سبحانه الكفار بأن إلههم إله واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth were originated with measured design; night and day succeed one another or differ in kind, color, and length.
rows.anchor: أي في إنشائهما مقدرين على سبيل الإختراع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships carry cargo and benefit people through travel, trade, and earnings; benefit is singled out because the list counts blessings, even though ships can also harm.
rows.anchor: والنفع بها يكون بركوبها والحمل عليها التجارات والمكاسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All exegetes take water from the sky as coming from the direction of heaven; another view says the intended source is clouds.
rows.anchor: من نحو السماء عند جميع المفسرين وقيل يريد به السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain makes dead land fertile after drought and failed growth; alternatively, it revives inhabitants by providing food and other necessities of life.
rows.anchor: وقيل أراد به إحياء أهل الأرض بإحياء الأقوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God disperses every kind of animal over the earth by creating animals in scattered places.
rows.anchor: فرق في الأرض من كل حيوان يدب وأراد بذلك خلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qatada explains varying winds as some bringing mercy and others punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل تصريفها بأن جعل بعضها يأتي بالرحمة وبعضها يأتي بالعذاب عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: When people cursed a strong wind, Ibn Abbas told them not to curse it but to ask that it be mercy rather than punishment.
rows.anchor: لا تسبوا الريح ولكن قولوا اللهم اجعلها رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds are controlled by God and moved as he wills from one land and place to another.
rows.anchor: يصرفها كما يشاء من بلد إلى بلد ومن موضع إلى موضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase people of understanding can include all rational people, whether or not they infer from the signs; another reading limits it to those who do infer.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه خاص بمن استدل به لأن من لم ينتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Change and susceptibility to increase or decrease show that the heavens and earth are originated; their origin implies a creator unlike them, since created bodies need an unoriginated maker and an infinite regress is impossible.
rows.anchor: تغير أجزائهما واحتمالهما الزيادة والنقصان وأنهما من الحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens' exact order and integration indicate a knowing, wise maker.
rows.anchor: على كون فاعلهما عالما حكيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regular cycles and changing lengths of night and day, tied to sun and moon, indicate a managing knower whose precise acts admit no disorder.
rows.anchor: وأخذ أحدهما من صاحبه الزيادة والنقصان وتعلق ذلك بمجاري الشمس والقمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water's delicacy allows ships to move, while winds drive them against the water's course; such provision for human benefit comes from a benefactor unlike humans or bodies.
rows.anchor: وتسخير الرياح لإجرائها في خلاف الوجه الذي يجري الماء إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain descends in separate drops, is held in the air despite water's downward nature, and falls in needed measure and season; this proves a powerful, wise administrator.
rows.anchor: ثم إمساكه في الهواء مع أن من طبع الماء الانحدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruits, plants, provisions, and animals display diverse tastes, colors, scents, benefits, and harms, demonstrating perfect power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: واختلاف مضارها ومنافعها في الأغذية والأدوية على كمال قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals' different forms and anatomies, with intricate tissues and organs, show their maker's power, wisdom, and beneficence.
rows.anchor: خالقا للذوات المختلفة بالهيئات المختلفة في التراكيب المتنوعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Winds vary by direction, heat, cold, gentleness, violence, barrenness, and pollination; no creature could change one direction into another.
rows.anchor: لو أجمع الخلق كلهم على أن يجعلوا الصبا دبورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds suspended without a cord or support prove the power of the incomparable God.
rows.anchor: لا يقدر على تسكين الأجسام بغير علاقة ولا دعامة إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phenomena evidence God's pre-eternity and eternity, perfect power, and marvelous creation: he is unmade, powerful, knowing, living, and untouched by change or affliction.
rows.anchor: استشهد بحدوث هذه الأشياء على قدمه وأزليته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge reaches even a speck in heaven or earth, and he is hearing and seeing.
rows.anchor: ولا يعرف عنه مثقال ذرة في الأرض ولا في السماء وهو السميع البصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs show God as benefactor, giver of incomparable blessings, and the only deity deserving worship.
rows.anchor: فيعلم بذلك أنه سبحانه الآله الذي لا يستحق العبادة سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse requires rational examination and inference as the path to knowing God, and invalidates reliance on imitation.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية أيضا دلالة على وجوب النظر والاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رفث here unambiguously means intercourse, though its original sense is indecent speech; the poet al-Ajjaj uses it for talk.
rows.anchor: الرفث الجماع هاهنا بلا خلاف وقيل: إن أصله القول الفاحش

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says إلى governs rafath because the word carries the sense of ifḍā, intimacy or reaching.
rows.anchor: إنما عديت بإلى في الأية لأنه بمعنى الإفضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clothing covers bodies; Arabs also call a wife clothing or a waist-wrapper, as the cited poetry witnesses.
rows.anchor: والعرب تسمي المرأة لباسا وإزارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اختيان is a form of betrayal; eye-treachery is furtive looking at what is forbidden, and the root concerns withholding a right.
rows.anchor: وخائنة الأعين مسارقة النظر إلى ما لا يحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Direct contact means skin touching skin; ابتغاء is seeking the desired thing.
rows.anchor: والمباشرة إلصاق البشرة بالبشرة وهي ظاهر الجلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The white thread is dawn's whiteness, the black thread night; day begins with the second, broader dawn.
rows.anchor: فأول النهار طلوع الفجر الثاني لأنه أوسع ضياء

rows.speaker: أبو داود
rows.claim: Abu Dawud's poem uses خيط to describe the streak of light at dawn.
rows.anchor: ولاح من الصبح خيط أنارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blackness of night explains such usages as whispered conversation, the dark complexion of Iraq's land, and a person's visible form; بيضة الإسلام means its foundation or protected core.
rows.anchor: والسواد والمساودة المسارة لأن الخفاء فيه كخفاء الشخص

rows.speaker: الطرماح
rows.claim: Al-Tirimmāḥ's verse describes women of the night keeping vigil as mourners; عكوف witnesses remaining in place.
rows.anchor: فبات بنات الليل في الليل عكفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: I'tikaf linguistically means staying put; in law it is remaining in a specified place for worship. God's boundaries are prohibitions and limits that prevent transgression.
rows.anchor: وهو في الشرع عبارة عن اللبث في مكان مخصوص للعبادة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines God's boundaries as what God forbids people to violate; the Arabic root of hadd is prevention or separation.
rows.anchor: هي ما منع الله من مخالفتها والحد جلد الزاني وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadd also names a sword's edge, a house boundary, or an end that keeps things from entering or leaving their proper bounds.
rows.anchor: والحد حد الدار والحد فرق بين الشيئين والحد نهاية الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report raised through Ali ibn Ibrahim's father to Abu Abd Allah says Ramadan nights initially barred eating after sleep, and intercourse was forbidden by night and day.
rows.anchor: كان الأكل محرما في شهر رمضان بالليل بعد النوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says the elderly fasting Mat'am ibn Jubayr slept before iftar when his wife was late with food; he thought eating was forbidden and later fainted while digging the trench, moving the Prophet to pity.
rows.anchor: وكان رجل من أصحاب رسول الله يقال له مطعم بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Young men secretly had intercourse at night in Ramadan, and the verse then permitted night intercourse and food after sleep until dawn.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله هذه الآية فأحل النكاح بالليل في شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: General transmitters give the Anṣari's name variously as Qays b. Sirma, Abu Sirma, Abu Qays b. Sirma, or Sirma b. Iyas; his long workday and missed iftar left him exhausted.
rows.anchor: واختلفت العامة في اسم هذا الرجل من الأنصار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi report that Qays told the Prophet he had worked all day, slept before eating, and awoke believing food forbidden; Umar and other men admitted comparable conduct, including intercourse after evening prayer.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس والسدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explains the fast's timing and rules: rafath means intercourse; Ibn Abbas treats rafath, clothing, direct contact, and ifḍā as euphemisms for it, while al-Zajjaj calls rafath a comprehensive term for a man's desires of a woman.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس إن الله سبحانه حيي يكني بما شاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the night singular refers to the nights of the month in which the following day is fasted; the wording implies intercourse had earlier been forbidden.
rows.anchor: والمراد بليلة الصيام الليلة التي يكون في غدها الصوم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far and Abu Abd Allah reportedly considered intercourse disliked on the first night of every month, except Ramadan's first night, when this verse makes it recommended; the author favors its generic application to all Ramadan nights.
rows.anchor: كراهية الجماع في أول ليلة من كل شهر إلا أول ليلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada interpret spouses as clothing because each is a source of rest and shelter for the other.
rows.anchor: أي هن سكن لكم وأنتم سكن لهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior rule forbidding intercourse and eating after sleep explains the phrase about betraying themselves: they sinned by violating it, so the later permission is a divine favor.
rows.anchor: علم الله أنكم كنتم تختانون أنفسكم لما حرم عليهم الجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation of self-betrayal is depriving oneself of lawful desire and pleasure by avoiding what had been prohibited.
rows.anchor: وقيل معنى تختانون تنقصون أنفسكم من شهواتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance here means either accepting their repentance or granting a concession and removing the former restriction; pardon means forgiveness or ending that prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه فرخص لكم وأزال التشديد عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to approach wives at night functions as permission to have intercourse.
rows.anchor: لفظه أمر ومعناه الإباحة

rows.speaker: الحسن وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and most exegetes read what God prescribed as offspring: one has intercourse hoping for a child who worships and praises God.
rows.anchor: أطلبوا ما قضى الله لكم من الولد عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes what God prescribed as lawful things stated in scripture; God loves people to accept his concessions as they accept obligations.
rows.anchor: اطلبوا ما كتب الله لكم من الحلال الذي بينه في كتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating and drinking are permitted until the true dawn makes day distinct from night; the comparison is with the threadlike first light, not its later spread.
rows.anchor: لأن القدر الذي يحرم الإفطار من البياض يشبه الخيط

rows.speaker: ابن دريد
rows.claim: Ibn Durayd takes مِن in مِن الفجر partitivally, meaning a portion of dawn; another grammatical analysis takes it as explanatory.
rows.anchor: أن يكون بمعنى التبعيض لأن المعنى من بعض الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Adi b. Hatim placed white and black hairs as literal threads to judge dawn; the Prophet laughed and explained that the words mean day and night.
rows.anchor: إني وضعت خيطين من شعر أبيض وأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fast ends when night begins, after sunset; as a precaution, one may wait for eastern redness to disappear and darkness to approach, while on flat land sunset suffices.
rows.anchor: فإذا غابت الشمس مع ظهور الآفاق في الأرض المبسوطة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Qatada limit forbidden contact during retreat to intercourse.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد به الجماع عن ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: مالك وابن زيد
rows.claim: Malik and Ibn Zayd include intercourse and all lesser intimacy such as kissing; the author says this is his school's position.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد الجماع وكل ما دونه من قبلة وغيرها عن مالك وابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His school permits i'tikaf only in the four named mosques; other jurists allow it in any mosque, while Malik requires a congregational mosque.
rows.anchor: المسجد الحرام ومسجد النبي ومسجد الكوفة ومسجد البصرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His school requires fasting for valid i'tikaf, as do Abu Hanifa and Malik; al-Shafi'i allows it without fasting.
rows.anchor: إلا بصوم، وبه قال أبو حنيفة ومالك وعند الشافعي يصح بغير صوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His school requires three days; Abu Hanifa requires a day, Malik ten days, and al-Shafi'i allows any length, even an hour.
rows.anchor: وعندنا لا يكون إلا في ثلاثة أيام، وعند أبي حنيفة يوم واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse bars sexual intimacy throughout the retreat, by night as well as by day, since the prohibition is attached to the state of i'tikaf.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية دلالة على تحريم المباشرة في الاعتكاف ليلا ونهارا

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets God's limits here as his sacred prohibitions; al-Dahhak calls them sins, and al-Zajjaj says they are what God forbids.
rows.anchor: حدود الله حرمات الله عن الحسن وقيل معناه معاصي الله عن الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not approach the limits means do not commit them; alternatively, do not violate God's obligations. The explanation aims to produce obedience to commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: أي فلا تأتوها وقيل معناه تلك فرائض الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shows that God intends all people to attain piety.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دلالة على أن الله تعالى أراد التقوى من جميع الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i assimilate the final sounds in لبثت; the remaining readers pronounce them separately.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي لبثت بالإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iraqi readers except Abu Amr and Asim omit the h in لم يتسن when continuing; others retain it in continuation, and all retain it at pause.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل العراق غير أبي عمرو وعاصم لم يتسن واقتد بحذف الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hijaz and Basra read ننشرها with shin and ra for reviving; Kufa and Syria read ننشزها with zay for raising; Aban from Asim has a rare ra reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أهل الحجاز والبصرة ننشرها بضم النون الأولى وبالراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i join the alif in قال اعلم and read a command; others separate it and read a declarative statement.
rows.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي قال اعلم موصولة الألف ساكنة الميم

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains assimilation by shared tongue-tip articulation and voicelessness; non-assimilation reflects the letters' different articulation groups.
rows.anchor: من أدغم لبثت أجرى التاء والثاء مجرى المثلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With h in لم يتسنه, possible accounts derive it from sanah as a root or from year-related forms, or connect the word to change as in المسنون; on pause-marker analyses h drops in connected speech.
rows.anchor: أن يكون الهاء لاما من السنه فيمن قال شجرة سنهاء

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو الشيباني
rows.claim: Abu Amr al-Shaybani is reported to derive the form from something changed or altered, comparing the change with a form in which sounds were transposed.
rows.anchor: وحكي أن أبا عمرو الشيباني إلى هذا كان يذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The h in اقتده may stand for the implied verbal noun, following the verb's meaning, rather than be a pausal h; the parallel is the source pronoun in 3:180.
rows.anchor: فبهديهم اقتده يكون اقتد الاقتداء فيضمر لدلالة الفعل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the verse, ننشرها means revive the bones; ننشزها means raise and fit them together, with نشوز also used when a wife withdraws from marital relations.
rows.anchor: ومن قرأ ننشزها بالزاء فالنشر الارتفاع

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: The imperative reading اعلم addresses the speaker himself after he witnessed the resurrection, as poets sometimes address themselves in the second person; Abu al-Hasan says it fits best.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: وهو أجود في المعنى

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-A'sha's line أنت بين القرو والعاصر addresses the poet himself as أنت, illustrating self-address in the imperative reading.
rows.anchor: وأنت بين القرو والعاصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خاوية means empty; a village is named for gathering residents, and خاوية على عروشها can mean its walls remain without roofs or that it lies fallen over its buildings.
rows.anchor: خاوية على عروشها أي بقيت حيطانها لا سقوف عليها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda interprets عروش as tents, the dwellings of nomads; another lexical view explains them as roofs or buildings.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة هي الخيام وهي بيوت الأعراب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنى asks from where or how; a year is a full cycle after winter and summer, while swimming and the verb لبث denote movement through water and remaining in place.
rows.anchor: وأنى يحيي من أين يحيي أو كيف يحيي والعام الحول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word حمار covers both domestic and wild asses; نشر is the opposite of folding and can also mean spreading news, scent, or a healing charm.
rows.anchor: والحمار يقال للوحشي والأهلي وأصله من الحمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial kaf coordinates the scene with Abraham's dispute; its syntactic position is accusative, and the passage expresses amazement because it exceeds ordinary cases.
rows.anchor: أو حرف عطف وهو عطف على معنى الكلام الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kaf may instead be emphatic extra wording, but the author prefers the first parsing because extra particles should not be posited without necessity.
rows.anchor: والأول أوجه لأنه لا يحكم بالزيادة إلا لضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنى is a question about the manner or kind of revival, not a denial that revival can occur; it may parse as a circumstantial accusative or verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وهذا أولى لأنه يكون سؤالا عن كيفية الإحياء لا إنكارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كم is the object of لبثت; the waw in ولنجعلك joins a suppressed verb, and كيف can modify the revival or the bones' state.
rows.anchor: دخلت الواو لاتصال اللام بفعل محذوف كأنه قال لنجعلك آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لم يتسنه means the food and drink were not altered by years; masculine singular can denote the generic food and drink, or the referent may be the nearer drink alone.
rows.anchor: أي لم تغيره السنون وإنما قال لم يتسنه على الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says the provisions were juice, figs, and grapes, unusually susceptible to spoiling, yet remained as freshly gathered.
rows.anchor: وهذه الثلاثة أسرع الأشياء تغيرا وفسادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkey's scattered bones demonstrate how long the man had been dead; he is asked to observe their restoration and the animal's revival.
rows.anchor: انظر إليه كيف تفرق أجزاوه وتبدد عظامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bones may be those of the donkey, according to al-Suddi and others, or the man's bones, according to al-Dahhak, Qatada, and al-Rabi'.
rows.anchor: فقيل أراد عظام حماره عن السدي وغيره

rows.speaker: الضحاك وقتادة والربيع
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak, Qatada, and al-Rabi' say the man's bones were revived; first his eye returned like the thin film on an egg, then scattered bones and meat reassembled until he and the donkey stood.
rows.anchor: قالوا أول ما أحيا الله منه عينه وهو مثل غرقيء البيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made him a sign for people as a proof of resurrection, either in answer to his request or through what happened to him and his donkey.
rows.anchor: أي حجة للناس في البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He learned the century had passed from God's miraculous signs in his body, food, drink, and donkey, and from worldly changes he saw on returning home.
rows.anchor: وإنما علم أنه مات مائة سنة بشيئين

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali reports that Uzayr left at fifty with a pregnant wife, died for a century, and returned still fifty while his son was a hundred years old.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي ع أن عزيرا خرج من أهله وامرأته حامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Nebuchadnezzar burned the Torah; Uzayr recited it from memory and produced a copy hidden in his grandfather's vineyard, matching it exactly, after which they said he was God's son.
rows.anchor: فأملأها من ظهر قلبه فقال رجل منهم حدثني أبي عن جدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أعلم means I know with certainty; the imperative reading is self-address or an order from God. He was not doubtful before, but witnessing made inferential knowledge immediate and certain.
rows.anchor: لم أقل ما قلت عن شك وارتياب ويحتمل أنه إنما قال ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabat refers to plants or vegetation; anbata is to make something grow, and related forms name adolescence, the poppy tree, and other growth.
rows.anchor: النبت الحشيش وكل ما ينبت من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sunbula follows a pattern related to sending something down; a grain-bearing ear is so called because its contents are covered like a hanging curtain.
rows.anchor: والأصل فيه الإسبال وهو إرسال الستر ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable can compare charitable spending with a grain, or compare the spenders with a sower; سبيل الله includes jihad and all forms of righteousness in the general view transmitted from Abu Abd Allah and chosen by Abu Ali al-Jubba'i.
rows.anchor: وسبيل الله هو الجهاد وغيره من أبواب البر كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A narrower view restricts spending in God's path here to jihad; on that view other devotional acts receive tenfold reward rather than this multiplication.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي خاصة بالإنفاق في الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image promises seven hundredfold reward, with God able to multiply even further or to grant this increase to whomever he wills.
rows.anchor: يعني أن النفقة في سبيل الله بسبعمائة ضعف

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that after this verse the Prophet prayed for a greater increase for his community; verses promising abundant multiplication and uncounted reward followed.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عمر أنه قال لما نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical yield of a hundred grains is possible even if unseen, as with imagined creatures in poetry and the Qur'anic image of devils' heads; millet supplies an actual example.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فقد رأى ذلك في الجاورس ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wide capacity means either power or mercy; Ali ibn Zayd explains all-knowing as knowing who deserves added reward or what intention motivates the spending.
rows.anchor: وقيل واسع الرحمة لا يضيق عن المضاعفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse connects to the invitation in 2:245; the intervening material is an exhortation and presentation of proofs, or the command to fight and finance those who reject the proofs, according to al-Zajjaj.
rows.anchor: اتصلت هذه الآية بقوله من ذا الذي يقرض الله قرضا حسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mann is reminding a recipient of a favor in a way that spoils it; its root means cutting off, as in an uncut reward or a frayed rope.
rows.anchor: المن هو ذكر ما ينغص المعروف كقول القائل أحسنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harm is injury that reaches its target; fear anticipates harm, and grief is distress that weighs heavily on the self.
rows.anchor: والأذى ضرر يتعجل وصوله إلى المضرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding spending, God describes proper giving as one that is not followed by reminders or injury; reminders include saying I gave you this or rescued you.
rows.anchor: والمن هو أن يقول له ألم أعطك كذا ألم أحسن إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harm may be insulting the recipient, frowning at him, burdening him with work, or diverting him to the donor's tasks; all spoil the gift and its reward.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون معنى الأذى أن يعبس وجهه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is recompense with God, secure from loss or diminution; the phrase at their Lord reassures the soul that what is with God cannot vanish.
rows.anchor: لأن ما عنده لا يخاف عليه فوت ولا نقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse makes the promise conditional: reward is deserved if spending is not followed by reminders or harm; without that condition, entitlement to reward does not follow.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أنه يصح الوعد بشرط

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: The Prophet says that the person who reminds others of a gift will not be addressed, regarded, or purified by God and will suffer painful punishment.
rows.anchor: وله عذاب أليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is ghani because he owns all things and can do all things; ghina is freedom from need, while ghina can also mean song or sufficiency.
rows.anchor: والله غني بأنه مالك لجميع الأشياء لأنه قادر عليها

rows.speaker: قيس بن الحطيم
rows.claim: Qays ibn al-Hatim uses غنيانها for a woman's singing in his verse.
rows.anchor: أجد بعمرة غنيانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gracious word means a kind, decent reply to a petitioner; other readings make it a good prayer, kind promise, or speech reconciling people.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه دعاء صالح نحو أن يقول صنع الله بك

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i interprets forgiveness as being spared sin and therefore safe from punishment; another view takes it as shielding the petitioner's request.
rows.anchor: أن معناه سلامة من المعصية لأن حالها كحال المغفرة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says forgiveness means the person asked to give pardons the petitioner for mistreatment, such as asking at a bad time, pressing, or entering without permission.
rows.anchor: أن معناه عفو المسؤول عن ظلم السائل عن الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kind words and pardon surpass a gift followed by harm because the injurious giver gains neither the money's benefit nor its afterlife reward, whereas kindness and pardon earn reward.
rows.anchor: لأن صاحب هذه الصدقة لا يحصل على خير لا على عين ماله

rows.speaker: محمد
rows.claim: A prophetic report says to let a petitioner finish before answering with dignity and gentleness, either a modest gift or gracious refusal, since unseen observers watch how God's gifts are used.
rows.anchor: إذا سأل السائل فلا تقطعوا عليه مسألته حتى يفرغ منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no charity or worship; he commands these acts for people's need of their reward.
rows.anchor: لم يأمركم بها ولا بشيء منها لحاجة منه إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forbearing and does not hasten punishment; in context this especially means he delays punishment for those who remind and harm recipients.
rows.anchor: لا يعاجلكم بالعقوبة وقيل لا يعجل بالعقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riya' derives from seeing and describes giving so others see it. صفوان is a smooth stone; al-Kisa'i gives its plural as صفي, while al-Mubarrad rejects that and uses صفا.
rows.anchor: وجمع في رئاء الناس بين همزتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of turab/dust relates to soil and poverty; ذا متربة is one seated in dust from need, and ترب can also mean a peer of the same age.
rows.anchor: مسكينا ذا متربة [البلد: 16] لأنه قعد على التراب للفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word at-taraib names chest bones; al-wabil is heavy rain, while the root of wabāl conveys severity and bad consequence.
rows.anchor: والوابل المطر الشديد الوقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted, unnamed poet uses صلد of hard smooth rock isolated from good; صلد also describes sterile ground, a miser, an unproductive flint, and things resistant to flow.
rows.anchor: ولا بصفا صلد عن الخير معزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kaf in كالذي is accusative as a circumstantial clause modifying the subject in تبطلوا.
rows.anchor: الكاف في قوله: { كالذي ينفق ماله } في موضع نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رئاء الناس is either a circumstantial expression describing the spender or a purpose for the spending.
rows.anchor: رئاء الناس مصدر وضع موضع الحال من الضمير في ينفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about dust describes the smooth stone; صلدا is a circumstantial state, and the inability clause also functions circumstantially.
rows.anchor: عليه تراب جملة في موضع جر بكونه صفة صفوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural verb they cannot refers to the generic class denoted by الذي, not to the singular wording.
rows.anchor: والواو عائد إلى معنى الذي لأنه جنس لا إلى لفظه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The likeness concerns both the boasting donor and hypocrite: when they perform a deed outside its commanded form, they earn no reward, which is what invalidating means.
rows.anchor: فإنهما إذا فعلا الفعل على غير الوجه المأمور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about reminders can mean boasting to the recipient or reminding God; injury is harm to the recipient.
rows.anchor: أي بالمنة على السائل وقيل بالمنة على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that God does not guide unbelievers to Paradise through their works, or does not grant them the extra care and success he gives believers.
rows.anchor: لا يعطيهم ما يعطي المؤمنين من زيادة الألطاف والتوفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asim and Ibn Amir read ربوة with fatḥa, most others with ḍamma, and Ibn Abbas has a rare kasra; Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and Abu Amr lighten أكلها while others double it.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم وابن عامر بربوة بفتح الراء والباقون بضمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author chooses the ḍamma form of ربوة, meaning a raised hill; أكل means produce or food rather than the act of eating, as 14:25 shows.
rows.anchor: والذي نختاره ربوة بضم الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thing's double can mean itself plus an equal, while its two doubles mean two equal amounts added; some use double to mean two times the original.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم ضعف الشيء مثلاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طل is light rain; the word also names blood left unavenged, a ruin's standing outline, or animal fat, all related to the image of dew or rain.
rows.anchor: والطل المطر الصغار يقال أطلت السماء فهي مطلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In syntax, seeking God's approval is a purpose, تثبيتا coordinates with it, the hill phrase modifies the garden, and the twofold produce describes its state.
rows.anchor: ابتغاء مرضاة الله مفعول له وتثبيتا معطوف عليه

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والسدي والشعبي
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, and al-Sha'bi explain تثبيتا من أنفسهم as strong conviction and insight in religion.
rows.anchor: بقوة اليقين والبصيرة في الدين عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Hasan and Mujahid say spenders confirm for themselves where their charity should be placed; the author answers that confirming themselves is itself a valid sense of making firm.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه أنهم يثبتون أين يضعون صدقاتهم

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Jubba'i reads تثبيتا as making oneself steadfast in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه وتوطينا لنفوسهم على الثبوت على طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A garden on high ground yields better and more than land receiving pooled runoff.
rows.anchor: لأن نبتها يكون أحسن وريعها أكثر من المستغل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavy rain gives the high garden twice the crop it would produce on ordinary lowland; the doubled yield may also mean two harvests yearly, six months apart.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون معناه مرتين في كل سنة واحدة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله
rows.claim: Abu Abd Allah explains the doubled produce as the multiplication of reward for spending to seek God's approval.
rows.anchor: معناه يتضاعف أجر من أنفق ماله مرضاة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if heavy rain does not reach it, the garden receives light rain and remains fruitful; its benefit is reliable in either case.
rows.anchor: أراد به أن خيرها لا يخلف على كل حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sees what people do and rewards them accordingly; alternatively, he knows who acts ostentatiously and who sincerely, a warning and encouragement.
rows.anchor: وقيل عالم بالمرائي والمخلص وفيه ترغيب وترهيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جنة is a densely planted garden; نخيل is sometimes explained from sifting and selecting, and نخلة names a date tree; the word may be masculine or feminine.
rows.anchor: والنخل جمع نخلة وهي شجرة التمر ويذكر ويؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An orchard has fruit trees and running waterways; كبير means age or magnitude, while كثير specifically implies number; إعصار is a twisting column of dust or wind.
rows.anchor: والإعصار غبار يلتف بين السماء والأرض كالتفاف الثوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأنهار names broad channels of flowing water; التحوت refers to people low under others' feet and unnoticed.
rows.anchor: والأنهار جمع النهر وهو المجرى الواسع من مجاري الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem compares a powerful whirlwind with another whirlwind, illustrating إعصار.
rows.anchor: إن كنت ريحا فقد لاقيت إعصارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression كبير differs from كثير: كبير describes size even for one house, whereas كثير necessarily implies number.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الكبير والكثير أن الكثير مضمن بعدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مِن in من نخيل explains the garden's type; the clause about running rivers can modify either the garden or the date palms, depending on the pronoun's antecedent.
rows.anchor: ومن في قوله { من نخيل } للتبيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable imagines an orchard of date palms and grapes, with water and every fruit, possessed by an aging person with weak, young children.
rows.anchor: أي أولاد صغار ناقصو القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إعصار is a powerful, upward-spinning wind column, commonly called a whirlwind; fire in it burns the garden.
rows.anchor: ريح شديدة تهب من الأرض نحو السماء مثل العمود

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi sees the ruined garden as the show-off in spending: he enjoys its benefit now but loses it when he most needs the reward in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: أنه مثل المرائي في النفقة لأنه ينتفع بها عاجلا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads the garden as the person who neglects obedience for worldly pleasures and thus faces especially bitter regret when he needs righteous deeds in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: أنه مثل للمفرط في طاعة الله تعالى بملاذ الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets it as someone whose work ends in corruption; the author says all three interpretations fit the verse.
rows.anchor: أنه مثل للذي يختم عمله بفساد عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation points back to charity, Abraham's story, the passerby at the ruined village, and all prior disclosures; God sets out religious proofs so people will reflect and understand.
rows.anchor: وقصة إبراهيم والذي مر على قرية وجميع ما سلف
